design_rationale: The study is a cluster-randomized trial in which nine Cree communities were randomly allocated to test (n = 5) or control (n = 4) conditions using an envelope-drawing randomization process.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization occurred at the cluster level prior to individual recruitment, which creates potential for identification/recruitment bias, and notable baseline imbalances were observed between the study groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was done over community radio with two 'rounds' of a constrained randomization process. Two baskets contained envelopes marked 'test' or 'control'... Randomization occurred prior to participant recruitment. However, despite the random assignment of communities, fewer test mothers had already delivered at time of enrollment (19.2% vs. 40.0%), had visited a dentist for toothache (35.5% vs. 50.0%), and had other children with a previous tooth extraction (34.1% vs. 48.9%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although mothers and interveners could not be blinded given the behavioral nature of the intervention, an intention-to-treat approach at the cluster/group level was followed for the primary outcome analysis and deviations reflect pragmatic implementation without evidence of unbalancing co-interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers and interveners were aware of their community's allocation... The primary statistical analysis was a comparison of caries prevalence in intervention and control groups, by a permutation test... with test statistic equal to the difference between caries prevalences in the two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was high and balanced across groups (110/127 [86.6%] in test vs. 131/145 [90.3%] in control), with reasons for loss (e.g., moved, lost contact) similar across arms and unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two hundred seventy-two mothers were recruited from the 5 test and 4 control communities... At trial's end, 241 children had follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary clinical outcome was assessed using standard validated criteria by examiners who were calibrated and masked to community allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: When each child was at least 30 mos old, clinical data were collected by calibrated examiners, masked to the community's assignment (Appendix). Criteria for caries detection were similar to those described by Pitts and co-workers (Pitts et al., 2001).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (ISRCTN41467632) and the prespecified primary outcome and statistical analysis were clearly reported without selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analysis outcome was enamel caries with substance loss (d2); no statistically significant treatment effect was detected... (clinical trial registration ISRCTN41467632).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to potential identification/recruitment bias and baseline imbalances stemming from participant recruitment occurring after cluster-level allocation, despite rigorous outcome blinding and pre-registered analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using a stratified blocked randomization design with a random number generator and allocation concealment via centralized telephone randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated using a random number generator with stratified blocks, concealed via telephone randomization prior to assignment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A stratified blocked randomization design employed a random number generator, with stratification based on the age of the mother. Randomly selected block sizes of 2 or 4 were used. Randomization was implemented by telephone between field staff enrolling the participants and a staff member at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. Field staff obtained informed consent and enrolled participants prior to obtaining group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and providers were aware of intervention assignment due to the nature of behavioral interventions, high fidelity and adherence were documented, protocol deviations were minimal, and an appropriate modified intention-to-treat analysis was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, providers and participants could not be masked in this trial... Modified intention-to-treat analyses were conducted. Eighty-eight percent of mothers completed at least 3 of 4 MI sessions offered.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up rates were high (>80% at 36 months, >90% contributing dental screening data) and balanced across groups with similar reasons for missingness, analyzed using mixed-effects models capable of handling missing at random data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 579 dyads (290 MI + ECS, 289 ECS) completed the baseline activities, and 84% completed the 36-mo assessment... Dyads included in analyses: 264 (91.0%) with ≥1 dental screening [in MI+ECS], 272 (94.1%) with ≥1 dental screening [in ECS].

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary clinical outcome was evaluated by trained, calibrated dental professionals who were successfully blinded to group assignment using standardized diagnostic criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, the licensed dental professionals, who collected primary outcome data through annual oral health screenings of the children, were blinded to group assignment... minimum tooth surface-level agreement between each calibrated examiner and the gold standard examiner was a Cohen's kappa ≥0.75.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial protocol and statistical analysis plan were pre-registered and previously published, and all pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes were reported in accordance with the planned analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01116726). Details of the trial design and protocol (Batliner et al. 2014) as well as caries assessment procedures (Warren et al. 2016) were previously published.

overall_summary: The randomized controlled trial was rigorously designed and conducted, with sound central randomization, blinded outcome assessors, high participant retention, and adherence to a pre-specified protocol and analysis plan. All five RoB 2 domains were evaluated as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using Zelen's design via manual simple randomization (drawing lots).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random sequence generation was done by drawing lots, details regarding allocation concealment are not described, and using drawing lots manually poses risks for allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random sequence generation was performed by manual (simple) randomization via drawing lots. Zelen's randomization with double consent was used to mitigate potential biases associated with disappointment bias. In Zelen's approach, randomization occurs before consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial analyzed participants using a per-protocol approach, excluding participants who declined or did not receive the intervention or did not complete follow-up, which can lead to substantial bias in estimating the effect of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main results are based on the per-protocol analyses. ... Participants allocated to the intervention group who declined to participate in the study received usual care but were excluded from the analysis. ... Fourth, our analyses were based on a per-protocol analysis, and not on an intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 27% of randomized participants had missing outcome data and exclusions occurred post-randomization without handling of missing data or sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 75 mother-child pairs included at baseline, 55 (73%) had a complete assessment after 12 months: 28 out of 40 (70%) in the intervention group and 27 out of 35 (77%) in the usual care group. ... Finally, the dropout rate was very high in both groups...

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes relied heavily on maternal self-report and unblinded clinical assessment, which are prone to detection and reporting bias given participants and assessors knew the assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, the outcome assessor was not blinded to group allocation, which could introduce some degree of detection bias. ... A structured questionnaire was completed by the mothers to obtain information on nutritional habits, socio-demographic and clinical variables.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered retrospectively, and the primary outcome was based on an author-created/modified score without a prospective protocol to confirm pre-specified analysis plans.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ...retrospectively registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials [ReBEC]: RBR-74qm3m. ... The primary outcome was the proportion of children classified as being at low risk of developing dental caries at the age of 12 months. We used a modified version of the Caries-risk Assessment Form of the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high due to substantial post-randomization attrition analyzed using a per-protocol strategy, high loss to follow-up, and subjective/self-reported outcome measures evaluated without blinding.

design_rationale: Participants were allocated to intervention and control groups using a randomized controlled trial design with a random number table (Zelen's design).

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation used a random number table before consent (Zelen's design), but 5 participants switched from control to intervention after learning about group allocation, and allocation concealment mechanisms prior to approaching participants were not fully detailed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Zelen's design with double consent and a random number table (11–13) was used to allocate women into test or control groups before their participation was sought... Only five women (0.8%) from all women recruited to the trial changed the group to which they were randomly allocated once they received information about the aims of the trial. All moved from the control group to the test group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was an educational health promotion programme where participant awareness of receiving materials is inherent, and there was no evidence of unintended deviations affecting trial results or differential non-protocol interventions between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intervention took the form of information provided to help mothers set up proper oral health habits early... Throughout the study women in the test group received three rounds of printed information applied in the form of anticipatory guidance.

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 30% of participants were lost to follow-up (208/649), with differential retention and evidence that missingness in the control group was significantly associated with risk-related prognostic factors (younger and less educated mothers).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The overall retention thorough to the examination was 70.6%, higher in the test group (74.4%) than in the control group (66.8%; Table 1)... In the control group losses to follow-up were higher among younger and less educated mothers (chi-square P < 0.01).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although visual criteria were standardized and an attempt was made to blind the examiner via receptionist scheduling, the sole examiner recruited participants, administered the intervention, and acknowledged that recall of group allocation could have compromised blinding for this partly subjective visual detection of noncavitated lesions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All children were examined by one of the authors (KP)... Thirdly, all mothers were recruited and the intervention administered by the same author as who conducted the dental examinations. Any recall of group assignment of individual mothers could have biased the dental observations.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or published protocol was reported to evaluate whether the specific primary outcome definition and regression models were pre-specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The differences in S-ECC incidence between the test and control groups, and the test subgroups were analysed... To calculate cumulative incidence of S-ECC, the definition of S-ECC suggested by the US National Institute of Health (6) was used.

overall_summary: The study is at overall high risk of bias primarily due to substantial missing outcome data (around 30% attrition) that was differential and significantly related to prognostic sociodemographic factors in the control group, accompanied by potential unblinding of the sole outcome assessor.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of two parallel groups using a computer-generated random number sequence with block randomization and allocation concealment via opaque sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated by an independent statistician and concealed using opaque sealed envelopes, with baseline characteristics balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random number sequence was generated in Excel by an independent statistician before recruitment. Randomization with a block size of 4 was adopted, and opaque sealed envelopes were used to conceal the allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and providers were not blinded due to the behavioral nature of the intervention, the protocol was delivered as intended without evidence of unplanned deviations or non-adherence affecting the trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, oral health education (OHE) providers and participants could not be masked during this trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was moderate over a 3-year follow-up period (approximately 25%), balanced between groups (22.4% test vs 27.3% control), and anticipated in the original sample size power calculations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 580 families participated in this clinical trial: 294 in the test group and 286 in the control group. At the 3-y-old toddler follow-up, 436 families (test, n = 228; control, n = 208) completed the data collection (75.2%; Appendix Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective clinical outcomes (visible plaque, white spot and cavitated lesions) and laboratory outcomes (PCR for S. mutans) were assessed by calibrated dental examiners blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, dental examiners who collected the clinical data were blinded to the participants' group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT02937194), and the reported outcomes align with standard pre-specified clinical and microbiological endpoints for this trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02937194

overall_summary: The randomized trial demonstrated low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains, with sound random allocation and concealment, blinded outcome assessment, balanced follow-up, and pre-registration.
